In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
iceberg supply to the abyssal Southern Ocean has been relatively constant during the past 0.7 m.y.
the mean accumulation rate for the residual ice-rafted debris has decreased during the past 700,000 yr.
iceberg calving in Antarctica is a relatively steady phenomenon, and the variations in the abundance of debris in the Southern Ocean reflect changes in the rate of melting of icebergs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the accumulation rates of ice-rafted detritus in the Southern Ocean are not a direct reflection of glacial activity in East Antarctica, and that the Southern Ocean is a dynamic system in which bottom-current activity may be as important as iceberg production in the distribution of detritus in abyssal sedi-ments.
the accumulation rates of Mn micronodules and ice-rafted debris are controlled by the same bottom-current processes.
the accumulation rate of icebergs in the Southern Ocean has not changed during the past 1 million yr, except for an interval of 100,00 yr.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Southern Ocean has been characterized by high-velocity Antarctic bottom water for the entire time span of the record, which extends back 690,000 years.

ice-rafted material in the Southern Ocean is subject to selective removal, and the amount of ice-rafted material deposited at the seafloor is a function of both iceberg flux and bottom-current velocity.
ice-rafted sediment accumulation rates in the abyssal Southern Ocean are strongly affected by winnowing processes.
